title: The derived two-open difference diagram has split local normal forms
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U,V$ be opens with $U\cup V=X$, and put $W=U\cap V$. Fix the four derived categories of module sheaves on $X,U,V,W$ in one morphism universe [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $r_U,r_V,r_W$ be the exact derived open restrictions, $s_U,s_V$ the exact overlap restrictions, and $e_U:r_U\mathbin{\star}s_U\cong r_W$, $e_V:r_V\mathbin{\star}s_V\cong r_W$ their canonical composition isomorphisms [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps], where $\star$ means first the left functor and then the right functor. Given $A\in D(\mathcal O_U)$, $B\in D(\mathcal O_V)$ and $c:s_U(A)\cong s_V(B)$, put $E=Rj_{U,*}A\oplus Rj_{V,*}B$ and $D=Rj_{W,*}(s_VB)$ using the derived direct images [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Then there exist $d:E\to D$, $p_U:r_U(E)\to A$, $p_V:r_V(E)\to B$ and $k:r_W(D)\to s_V(B)$ such that $(p_U,r_U(d)):r_U(E)\to A\oplus r_U(D)$ and $(p_V,r_V(d)):r_V(E)\to B\oplus r_V(D)$ are isomorphisms and $e_{U,E}^{-1};s_U(p_U);c-e_{V,E}^{-1};s_V(p_V)=r_W(d);k$, where the semicolon denotes composition in execution order. The two objects are these fixed direct-image constructions. This constructs only their difference diagram; it neither chooses a fiber of $d$ nor asserts an object restricting to $A$ and $B$.

proof.text: Derive the exact open restriction/direct-image adjunctions, using [def-pc-derived-direct-image] and [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps]. Their underived counits are invertible; direct image is fully faithful and preserves K-injectives as a right adjoint of exact restriction, so its right derived functor is fully faithful and the derived counits are invertible. Define pU and pV by projection followed by these counits. Set t=eU.inv;sU(pU);c minus eV.inv;sV(pV), define d=adjW.homEquiv(t), and k=adjW.counit. The inverse law of homEquiv proves t=rW(d);k. All maps and objects are constructed explicitly.

proof.text: For the two individual summands let f be the W-adjoint of eU.inv;sU(adjU.counit) and g the W-adjoint of eV.inv;sV(adjV.counit). Apply [lem-sc-derived-open-intersection-mate-iso] with (O,P)=(V,U) and (U,V) to obtain invertibility of rV(f) and rU(g). Naturality of eU,eV, the biproduct identities, and homEquiv naturality prove inl;d=f;RjW(c) and inr;d=-g. Additivity of RjW follows from the derived adjunction.

proof.text: After the preserved biproduct comparison, (pU,rU(d)) is triangular with invertible diagonal (adjU.counit,-rU(g)). A triangular matrix with invertible diagonal factors as a diagonal isomorphism followed by an explicitly invertible unipotent matrix. On V swap the summands and use diagonal (adjV.counit,rV(f);rV(RjW(c))). This is invertible because c is an isomorphism. The three private matrix lemmas are fully proved from Mathlib. Retain the caller covering hypothesis unchanged although the construction does not use it.
